events.event: Exa launches Agent Ultra, the highest-effort deep-research mode of Exa Agent

facts.fact: Exa launched Agent Ultra, a deep-research and list-building mode of Exa Agent; launch post dated 2026-09-25 (changelog 2026-09-24).
Exa-run WANDR result: Agent Ultra 81.4% soft recall vs 72.3% for Opus 5.5 (9.1 points; Exa calls it +12.6%).
Other Exa-run results: DeepSearchQA 93.9% F1, WideSearch 58.9% row-level F1, Find-All Company 2,451 passing entities per task vs 146 for Opus 5.5.
Exa claims Ultra costs about half as much per task as Opus 5.5 on WANDR and 46% less per task than GPT-6 Astra on DeepSearchQA.
Ultra runs typically take about 30 minutes on complex tasks and up to 3 hours on very hard ones.
Runs are capped at $20 by default, adjustable $1-$100 (maxCostDollars), with an optional 300-10,800 s limit (maxDurationSeconds).
Exa co-founder Jeff Wang says Ultra uses heavy agent parallelization, code execution and a database tool, orchestrated by frontier models (X, 2026-09-25).

events.event: Exa launches Exa Snapshot (research preview) for point-in-time web search

facts.fact: Exa Snapshot adds snapshotAsOf to /search and /contents, returning pages as they existed at a chosen date; launched 2026-09-17 as a research preview.
Exa says Snapshot draws on over 400 billion webpage snapshots spanning about two decades.

events.event: AIMultiple publishes DR-20 deep-research benchmark that includes Exa Agent

facts.fact: On AIMultiple's DR-20 Bench (20 business research briefs, blind-graded), Exa Agent scored 0.584, fourth of five, below Codex CLI 0.790, Claude Code 0.775 and Grok CLI 0.699; statistically tied with Gemini CLI 0.565.
Exa Agent cost $1.00 per task ($20 total API spend) vs $13.38-$18.35 for the two leaders, and fully reproduced 89 of 434 required facts vs 202 for Claude Code.

events.event: Perplexity launches Fast Search in its Search API, built on the Photon engine

facts.fact: Perplexity launched Fast Search in its Search API, running on Photon, a new Rust retrieval and ranking engine; 95% of results return in 230 ms or less.
Fast Search costs $1 per 1,000 requests vs $5 for standard web search.
Perplexity reports Fast Search single-call latency of 160 ms at p50 (230 ms at p95).
Perplexity says the fast preset cut estimated model-plus-search cost per task by 68% vs its default preset across six agentic benchmarks, at comparable quality.
Perplexity concedes lower quality for the fast preset: relevance (DCG) 2.21 vs 2.45 and answer availability 56.7% vs 59.6% for the default preset.
Photon claims: p99 retrieval-and-ranking latency down from about 800 ms to 65 ms, about 20% fewer serving machines, 2.5x more data per document.
Perplexity says Photon was built by a small engineering team working with hundreds of agents.
Shopify's Mikhail Parakhin says Shopify measures all search APIs and Perplexity has become its main one 'on merit' (X, 2026-09-24).
Perplexity Fast Search is now built into Hermes Agent for Nous Portal users; Nous Research says it is free on all Portal tiers.
